scope: Static search across four analyzed executables. Negative findings are limited to code/resources in those executables; an external tool or build-time-only harness is not excluded.

senders.result: no hidden tool IDs in any build; only Reset and Exit are registered
present only on tool windows after open; local IDs invoke editor actions and are not global opener IDs
senders.coverage: Particle, Egg, Marker, Broker, Flow, generic editor roots in all builds

senders.result: none of the hidden global IDs occur as dialog control IDs
no RT_ACCELERATOR resources; no CreateAcceleratorTable, TranslateAccelerator, RegisterHotKey, GetKeyState, or GetAsyncKeyState code xrefs found
senders.coverage: all four PE resources and imported/referenced API call sites

senders.result: CreateMenu/CreatePopupMenu, InsertMenuItemA, SetMenu, CheckMenuItem, DestroyMenu are used; AppendMenu, LoadMenu, TrackPopupMenu/Ex are absent by code xref
many control messaging sites exist, but no site was found constructing WM_COMMAND 0x111 with a hidden global tool ID; PostMessage sites do not construct those IDs
senders.coverage: all SendMessageA/PostMessageA references and immediate/dataflow candidates

senders.result: main WndProc routes WM_COMMAND and selected paint/close messages, not WM_KEYDOWN/WM_SYSKEYDOWN; game DirectInput has no demonstrated path to editor command IDs
senders.coverage: main WndProc and key API audit

senders.mechanism: external development harness or other process
senders.result: not established or excluded by executable analysis

conclusion: No original in-executable command sender for hidden editor/tool openers has been recovered. Classify those commands D, not dead code. This does not prove how Steel Monkeys reached them in a separate development environment.
